A high outcrop among old pines, the rock pale with lichen, the trees pressing in on three sides, the fourth opening onto a long view down a forested valley, ridges receding in diminishing layers of grey-blue.

A tangled deadfall deep in the wood, enormous fallen trunks crossing one another at angles, the whole structure colonised by moss and bracket fungus, a fox den visible beneath the largest root mass in the failing light.

A hidden grove of rowans at the edge of an upland forest, their berries burning orange against dark foliage, the ground soft with wet grass, cloud shadow moving fast overhead, the treeline close behind and the valley falling away ahead.
A mossy forest path winding between colossal moss-draped trunks, shafts of amber light falling between them, the deep wood receding into green-gold haze, roots buckling the earth underfoot.
The pebbled edge of a clear forest creek, water sliding over smooth stones in bright ribbons, ferns crowding both banks, dappled light shifting on the surface with every breeze.
A rocky ledge jutting over an endless misty canopy, the forest rolling away below in layered green-grey haze, distant ridgelines fading to blue, the treetops breathing in slow wind.
The still shore of a moonlit forest lake, the water a black mirror holding the full moon entire, reeds standing at the margin, mist curling slowly off the glassy surface.
The foot of a tiered waterfall plunging into a clear pool, spray hanging in the air like smoke, wet black rock glistening, hanging moss trembling with every crash of white water.
Ancient stone ruins swallowed by ivy deep in the forest, cracked walls tilted by root and time, filtered green light pooling on mossy flagstones, the trees pressing close on every side.
A sunlit fern glade opening among the trees, the ground a rolling sea of bright green fronds, a single shaft of light striking the centre, the forest wall dark and dense beyond.
A misty wooded ravine crossed by a mossy log bridge, the creek far below glinting through fog, ferns spilling from every crevice, the trees on both walls leaning inward overhead.
A broad forest riverbank of smooth pale stones, the river running wide and dark between wooded shores, willows trailing their fingers in the current, the far bank lost in afternoon haze.
A high cliff face overlooking rolling forested hills, the canopy an unbroken green ocean beneath, hawks circling level with the ledge, the tree line climbing the cliff's own base in walls of oak.

A hollow beneath the forest floor where bioluminescent mushrooms cast cold blue-violet light on the roots above, the air thick with spores and silence, the entrance a dark gap between two fallen trunks.

A frost-rimed winter wood at dawn, every branch and twig glittering with white crystal, breath fogging in the still cold air, pale light slanting low between silver birches, the snow unbroken underfoot.
A bluebell-carpeted spring grove, the forest floor a wash of soft violet-blue to every edge, the canopy only just leafing out in pale green, light falling freely through the thin new growth above.
A deep autumn wood of russet, amber, and burning gold, leaves spiralling down in slow eddies, the forest floor thick with colour, a low mist sitting between the trunks in the early morning cold.
A woodland marsh of black water and sunken roots, pale wisps drifting between the drowned trunks, sedge and bog-moss on every hammock, the tree canopy above reflected in dark still pools below.

A cathedral grove of ancient yews, their trunks twisted into vast dark columns, the canopy so dense the light is perpetual green dusk, red berries bright against the shadows, the silence total and heavy.

A willow-overhung river-bend pool, the long curtains of pale green trailing into slow dark water, the bank soft with sedge and clover, sunlight breaking in fragments on the rippled surface beneath the branches.

A dim forest hollow where a clear spring rises from bare rock, the water perfectly still before overflowing in a thin bright thread, moss thick on every stone, the surrounding trees dripping quietly overhead.

A switchback trail climbing a forested ridge, the trees crowding both sides in walls of oak and hornbeam, the valley glimpsed below through gaps in the canopy, the path soft with decades of leaf-fall.

A storm-felled giant lying across the forest floor, its root-plate rearing up taller than the surrounding trees, a whole corridor of sky opened above the gap, new saplings already racing upward through the light.

A hidden forest pool fed by underground seepage, perfectly circular, the water dark and still, ringed entirely by ancient moss-covered stones and overarching hazel, not a ripple on the surface, the air cool and hushed.

A cedar forest in deep shade, the trunks rising straight as pillars into a canopy that blocks all but faint greenish light, the ground bare of undergrowth, the air resinous and cool, silence absolute.

A forest edge where open grassland presses against a wall of old oak, the last great trees casting long shadows across the meadow, ivy thick on their lower trunks, the deep wood visible in the darkness between them.

A rocky stream gorge cutting through dense forest, the water white over boulders ten feet below, the gorge walls hung with liverwort and dripping fern, the trees arching overhead to nearly close the gap of sky.

A high forest outcrop of bare granite rising through the canopy, lichen-covered and windswept, the surrounding treetops at knee level, the full sweep of the forested valley below visible in every direction beneath a wide open sky.
